title: == vs ===: the quiet bug maker
why_it_matters: Loose equality gives odd results that are hard to spot.
explanation: === compares value and type. == quietly converts types first, so strange things become true, like 0 == false. Use === everywhere, and you only have to remember one set of rules.
code:
console.log(5 == "5");     // true (surprise)
console.log(5 === "5");    // false
console.log(0 == false);   // true
console.log(0 === false);  // false
try_it: Search your code for == and replace each one with ===.
